html:
SMTO-CTX-0017 — SMTO couldn't continue this task in a new conversation

GUID: 30b00851-5988-4516-92be-1ca9fdf6e58c
Slug: task-context-capture-failed
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: ctx

What happened

  • When you chose to continue this task in a new conversation, SMTO couldn't gather the task's saved details to bring along. No new conversation was made, and the original task is unchanged.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the original task and check that its attached files and results still show and open. SMTO copies these into the new conversation, and a missing item can stop the copy.
  2. Select Continue in new conversation on the task again. No conversation was made the first time, so trying again won't create a duplicate.
  3. If it still fails, start a new conversation yourself and paste the key details of the original task into your first message. This lets you keep working while the saved details are looked into.

What success looks like

  • A new conversation opens with a card that says Continued from previous conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details if it's shown, or note the time it happened, and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete the original task or its files; it holds the history the new conversation would copy.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The task-fork route caught a ValueError while capturing the source task's saved continuation context; the wrapper does not record which capture step failed, and the transaction created no conversation.

What this means

  • The task-fork route caught a ValueError while building the saved continuation context; this wrapper does not identify one specific capture cause. Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • The task-fork route caught a ValueError while building the saved continuation context; this wrapper does not identify one specific capture cause.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the fork failure's retained cause and source task eligibility; distinguish missing scope from snapshot-size or validation failure.

How to fix it

  • Check the Server log for the ValueError behind the task fork request (POST /api/agent/chats/.../tasks/.../fork, handled by TaskForkService.create, build_snapshot and capture in api/agent_ui_support/task_fork.py). Restore access to the source run's saved state, receipts and context assets, then repeat the fork with the same client_submission_id.
  • Keep the original run and receipts. Restore access to its saved context before using the supported continuation flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported fork flow creates a valid saved-context snapshot linked to the intended source task.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
